title: How to keep your Claude chats and Google files private
excerpt: Some ‘private’ chats and docs are showing up on search engines. Here’s how to protect yours
content_html:
Users of Anthropic’s Claude chatbot were surprised over the weekend to learn that some of their conversations may be discoverable on search engines like Google and Bing. The revelation is raising questions about how much control people actually have over what they share online.

Anthropic allows Claude users to create public links to their chat threads, which gives anyone with the link the ability to view their conversations – similar to sharing options on apps like Google Docs. But what users may not have realized was that means their Claude conversations, however sensitive or personal, could show up in public search results.

As of Tuesday morning, no Claude chats appeared in Google or Bing in searches that reportedly previously surfaced them. Still, the discovery has forced users of chatbots like Claude and other online services to confront some important questions: what does it mean to make your chats shareable? When are your personal files public for all to see? And what can you do about it?

The uproar over Claude chats showing up in search results began on Sunday, after Reddit users discovered that typing “site:claude.ai/share” on Google or Bing pulled up chat logs that included personal conversations. Once users create publicly shareable links to their chats, chat logs are public and may become discoverable on search engines. So users intending to share content with a small group of people may inadvertently share their chat with the entire internet.

This isn’t the first time chats have shown up in Google results. After a similar incident in September, Anthropic told Forbes that chats became visible via Google and Bing search because they were shared online or on social media. It also said it uses a “robots.txt” file, a set of instructions that tell search engines what they can and cannot log, to prevent the issue.

Both Google and Bing instruct developers and page owners like Anthropic to take additional measures like inserting a “noindex” HTML tag, which prevents web crawlers from surfacing pages in search results. Many of the chats that appeared in Google search results didn’t have that tag, according to Wired, which reviewed several before they were taken down. Anthropic did not respond to questions about whether they had added the tag to shared links.

Anthropic declined to comment but previously told other publications it does not share chat directories or sitemaps with search engines.

How to protect your content

Users may want to check their sharing settings on other platforms as well.

The Guardian US used a similar search query to look up Google documents that users have created public links for and found a long list of files, including many with sensitive information.

Typing in a site-specific search query for Google Drive files with the word “test” turned up several pages of Google documents ranging from exams from specific elementary and high schools to the results of lead and radon detector tests in specific locations.

Searches for documents containing the word “confidential” surfaced files with potentially sensitive or private information including a city health department confidentiality agreement. It’s unclear how long these documents have been available online, but some files date back to 2003. Google spokesperson Ross Richendrfer said these documents were discoverable because the links had been posted somewhere on the internet or social media.

Neither Google nor Anthropic warn users their files could be indexed by search engines when creating shareable links. These companies need to be clearer with their users about the implications, said Jacob Hoffman-Andrews, a senior staff technologist at digital privacy advocacy group the Electronic Frontier Foundation.

“The privacy afforded by ‘anyone with a link’-style sharing of chats and documents is fragile,” Hoffman-Andrews said. “If you share something with a friend, and they share it with a friend, and they post it to social media, suddenly it’s findable and readable by anyone on the web.”

Users should use “extreme caution” when creating shareable links or take an alternative approach like copying and pasting the text or screenshotting instead, he added.

Fortunately, you can unpublish chats or Google files you’ve previously shared.

On Claude’s desktop browser, click your profile icon on the bottom-left corner and choose “settings” from the menu. Navigate to the “privacy” tab, scroll down to the “your data” section and click “manage” public chats. From there, you can delete those public threads.

On Google Drive, you’ll have to open each individual document you’ve made public. Click the “share” button on the top right of your desktop browser window and then change your “general access” settings from “anyone with the link” to “restricted” or specified people, groups or spaces.

The visibility of both the chats and the Google documents on search engines serves as a reminder to be cautious about what information you really want to share with “anyone with the link”.

“Designing to incentivize viral sharing can also lead to users unintentionally oversharing,” said Hoffman-Andrews.

content_html_zh:
Anthropic 的 Claude 聊天机器人的用户周末惊讶地发现，他们的一些对话可能可以在 Google 和 Bing 等搜索引擎上发现。 这一揭露引发了人们对人们在网上分享的内容实际上拥有多少控制权的疑问。

Anthropic 允许 Claude 用户创建指向其聊天线程的公共链接，这使任何拥有该链接的人都能够查看他们的对话 - 类似于 Google Docs 等应用程序上的共享选项。 但用户可能没有意识到，这意味着他们与克劳德的对话，无论多么敏感或私人，都可能会出现在公共搜索结果中。

截至周二上午，据报道，谷歌或必应搜索中没有出现克劳德的聊天记录。 尽管如此，这一发现还是迫使 Claude 等聊天机器人和其他在线服务的用户面临一些重要问题：让聊天内容可共享意味着什么？ 您的个人档案什么时候公开供所有人查看？ 你能做些什么呢？

周日，Reddit 用户发现在 Google 或 Bing 上输入“site:claude.ai/share”会调出包含个人对话的聊天记录后，搜索结果中出现的 Claude 聊天记录引起了轩然大波。 一旦用户创建了可公开共享的聊天链接，聊天日志就会公开，并且可能会在搜索引擎上被发现。 因此，打算与一小群人共享内容的用户可能会无意中与整个互联网共享他们的聊天内容。

这并不是聊天内容第一次出现在 Google 结果中。 在 9 月份发生类似事件后，Anthropic 告诉《福布斯》，聊天内容通过 Google 和 Bing 搜索可见，因为它们是在网上或社交媒体上共享的。 它还表示，它使用“robots.txt”文件，这是一组指令，告诉搜索引擎可以记录什么和不能记录什么，以防止出现此问题。

Google 和 Bing 都指示开发人员和 Anthropic 等页面所有者采取额外措施，例如插入“noindex”HTML 标签，以防止网络爬虫在搜索结果中显示页面。 据《连线》报道，谷歌搜索结果中出现的许多聊天内容都没有这个标签，该公司在删除之前对其中几条内容进行了审查。 Anthropic 没有回答有关他们是否已将标签添加到共享链接的问题。

Anthropic 拒绝置评，但此前曾告诉其他出版物，它不会与搜索引擎共享聊天目录或站点地图。

如何保护您的内容

用户可能还想检查其他平台上的共享设置。

美国卫报使用类似的搜索查询来查找用户为其创建了公共链接的谷歌文档，并发现了一长串文件，其中许多包含敏感信息。

在针对 Google Drive 文件的特定站点搜索查询中输入“测试”一词，会出现几页 Google 文档，范围从特定小学和高中的考试到特定地点的铅和氡气探测器测试结果。

搜索包含“机密”一词的文件会显示包含潜在敏感或私人信息（包括城市卫生部门保密协议）的文件。 目前还不清楚这些文件在网上发布了多久，但有些文件可以追溯到 2003 年。 谷歌发言人罗斯·里琴德弗（Ross Richendrfer）表示，这些文件是可以被发现的，因为这些链接已经发布在互联网或社交媒体上的某个地方。

Google 和 Anthropic 都没有警告用户在创建可共享链接时他们的文件可能会被搜索引擎索引。 数字隐私倡导组织电子前沿基金会的高级技术专家雅各布·霍夫曼·安德鲁斯 (Jacob Hoffman-Andrews) 表示，这些公司需要让用户更清楚地了解其影响。

霍夫曼-安德鲁斯说：“‘任何有链接的人’式的聊天和文件共享所提供的隐私是脆弱的。” “如果你与朋友分享某些内容，他们也与朋友分享，并将其发布到社交媒体上，突然之间，网络上的任何人都可以找到并阅读该内容。”

他补充说，用户在创建可共享链接时应“极其谨慎”，或者采取替代方法，例如复制和粘贴文本或屏幕截图。

幸运的是，您可以取消发布之前共享的聊天或 Google 文件。

在克劳德的桌面浏览器上，单击左下角的个人资料图标，然后从菜单中选择“设置”。 导航到“隐私”选项卡，向下滚动到“您的数据”部分，然后单击“管理”公共聊天。 从那里，您可以删除这些公共线程。

在 Google 云端硬盘上，您必须打开您公开的每个单独文档。 单击桌面浏览器窗口右上角的“共享”按钮，然后将“一般访问”设置从“知道链接的任何人”更改为“受限”或指定的人员、群组或空间。

聊天记录和谷歌文档在搜索引擎上的可见性提醒您要谨慎对待您真正想与“知道链接的任何人”共享哪些信息。

霍夫曼-安德鲁斯说：“旨在激励病毒式分享的设计也可能导致用户无意中过度分享。”
